description: Assesses the appropriate networking and edge protection strategy based on service type, data sensitivity, user base, and availability requirements.

recommendation.pattern: CDN with WAF and DDoS Protection
recommendation.rationale: Public-facing services with large user bases require edge protection including a Content Delivery Network for performance, a Web Application Firewall for security, and DDoS mitigation. This layered approach protects the origin while improving user experience through caching and geographic distribution.

operationalBurden.staffingImplications: Requires security team involvement for WAF rule management; CDN configuration needs performance engineering input
operationalBurden.ongoingMaintenance: WAF rule updates, certificate rotation, cache invalidation strategy, and DDoS response procedures

costConsiderations.runningCosts: CDN costs based on data transfer and requests; WAF costs based on rules and requests; DDoS protection may have fixed monthly cost
costConsiderations.transitionCosts: DNS migration; CDN configuration; WAF rule development and testing

recommendation.pattern: Private Network with Zero Trust Access
recommendation.rationale: Internal services handling sensitive data should use private networking with zero trust principles. This means no implicit trust based on network location; every request is authenticated and authorised regardless of source. Private endpoints eliminate public internet exposure.

operationalBurden.staffingImplications: Requires network engineering expertise; zero trust implementation needs security architecture input
operationalBurden.ongoingMaintenance: Network policy reviews, access rule updates, connectivity monitoring, and security posture assessment

costConsiderations.runningCosts: Private endpoint costs; VPN/ExpressRoute costs; zero trust platform licensing
costConsiderations.transitionCosts: Network redesign; zero trust implementation; application changes for private endpoints

recommendation.rationale: API services with external integrations require network segmentation to isolate external-facing components from internal systems. An API gateway at the network boundary provides a controlled entry point with rate limiting, authentication, and request validation.

operationalBurden.staffingImplications: Requires network and security team collaboration; API gateway configuration needs developer input
operationalBurden.ongoingMaintenance: Certificate rotation, IP whitelist updates, security group reviews, and gateway scaling

costConsiderations.runningCosts: Load balancer and gateway costs; data processing charges; certificate management
costConsiderations.transitionCosts: Network architecture design; security group configuration; testing with external partners

recommendation.pattern: Multi-AZ Network Architecture with Redundant Connectivity
recommendation.rationale: Services requiring very high availability need network architecture spanning multiple availability zones with redundant connectivity paths. This eliminates single points of failure at the network layer and ensures service continuity during zone-level failures.

operationalBurden.staffingImplications: Requires senior network engineer; multi-AZ architecture adds complexity to troubleshooting
operationalBurden.ongoingMaintenance: Failover testing, routing table management, connectivity monitoring, and capacity planning across zones

costConsiderations.runningCosts: Cross-AZ data transfer costs; redundant connectivity charges; global accelerator fees
costConsiderations.transitionCosts: Network architecture redesign; multi-AZ deployment; failover testing

recommendation.rationale: Without cloud access, networking relies on traditional on-premises infrastructure with perimeter-based security. While zero trust principles should still be applied where possible, the implementation will use physical and virtual network segmentation with firewalls and intrusion detection.

operationalBurden.staffingImplications: Requires dedicated network operations team; physical infrastructure management
operationalBurden.ongoingMaintenance: Firmware updates, firewall rule management, certificate management, and capacity planning

costConsiderations.runningCosts: Hardware maintenance contracts; licensing; staffing; power and cooling

defaultRecommendation.rationale: When no specific conditions strongly favour an alternative, a managed load balancer with WAF provides basic edge protection suitable for most government services. This handles TLS termination, basic DDoS protection, and request routing without complex configuration.

candidateTechnologies.name: Google Cloud Load Balancing + Cloud Armor

operationalBurden.staffingImplications: Standard development team can manage basic configuration
operationalBurden.ongoingMaintenance: Certificate rotation and health check configuration

costConsiderations.runningCosts: Moderate; based on data processed and connection count
costConsiderations.transitionCosts: DNS configuration and TLS certificate setup

commonQuestions: Is the service internet-facing or internal only?
What DDoS protection level is required?
Are there specific IP whitelisting requirements?
Is there existing network infrastructure to integrate with?
What are the latency requirements for end users?
Is there a requirement for geographic distribution?
evidenceNeeded: Network architecture diagram showing connectivity requirements
Traffic flow analysis including expected bandwidth
Latency requirements and user geographic distribution
artefactsToProduce: Firewall and security group rules specification
